Canada's defence policy, Our North, Strong and Free: A Renewed Vision for Canada's Defence [C4, C6, C7], describes AI-enabled modernization as part of the digitalization of defence. [C4] The policy states that the Canadian Armed Forces is updating its tools and processes to better suit them to the modern world. [C4] It also mentions that Canada will make full use of its digital technologies by overhauling outdated and analog processes to improve its ability to hire people, conduct security screening, and share information in a timely way. [C4] This includes expanding the use of artificial intelligence-driven data management tools, as well as initiatives to advance big data management, acquire analytical tools, and expand cloud-based computing on open and secure networks. [C4]

The DND/CAF AI Strategy, The Department of National Defence and Canadian Armed Forces Artificial Intelligence Strategy [C1, C10, C11, C2, C3, C5, C8, C9], describes AI-enabled modernization as a necessary step to ensure that Canada can continue to share a common operating picture with its allies. [C2] The strategy states that AI is transforming the defence environment and that it has enabled new operational and corporate capabilities to help Canada continue to meet its obligations to protect and defend the country and its citizens. [C2] It also mentions that AI is not a standalone technology but part of a broader and even more transformative technological revolution brought about by the convergence of data and digital with AI. [C2] The strategy commits the Defence Team to becoming AI-enabled by 2030, in line with its goals for an overall digital transformation by that date. [C2, C5]

Both documents emphasize the importance of AI-enabled modernization for Canada's defence [C1, C10, C11, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, C7, C8, C9] and highlight the need for Canada to adopt AI to maintain its operational advantage and interoperability with its allies. [C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C8] However, the DND/CAF AI Strategy provides a more detailed and specific plan for achieving AI-enabled modernization, including the creation of a DND/CAF AI Centre [C1, C10] (DCAIC) [C1, C10, C11] and the development of a staged implementation plan with timelines, milestones, and performance indicators. [C8]

**Sources:**
- Our North, Strong and Free: A Renewed Vision for Canada's Defence, pages 22-23, 32, 35 [C4, C6, C7]
- The Department of National Defence and Canadian Armed Forces Artificial Intelligence Strategy, pages 1-3, 6-10, 12-15, 20, 27 [C1, C10, C11, C2, C3, C5, C8, C9]

content_blocks.text:
Canada's defence policy, Our North, Strong and Free: A Renewed Vision for Canada's Defence, describes AI-enabled modernization as part of the digitalization of defence. The policy states that the Canadian Armed Forces is updating its tools and processes to better suit them to the modern world. It also mentions that Canada will make full use of its digital technologies by overhauling outdated and analog processes to improve its ability to hire people, conduct security screening, and share information in a timely way. This includes expanding the use of artificial intelligence-driven data management tools, as well as initiatives to advance big data management, acquire analytical tools, and expand cloud-based computing on open and secure networks.

The DND/CAF AI Strategy, The Department of National Defence and Canadian Armed Forces Artificial Intelligence Strategy, describes AI-enabled modernization as a necessary step to ensure that Canada can continue to share a common operating picture with its allies. The strategy states that AI is transforming the defence environment and that it has enabled new operational and corporate capabilities to help Canada continue to meet its obligations to protect and defend the country and its citizens. It also mentions that AI is not a standalone technology but part of a broader and even more transformative technological revolution brought about by the convergence of data and digital with AI. The strategy commits the Defence Team to becoming AI-enabled by 2030, in line with its goals for an overall digital transformation by that date.

Both documents emphasize the importance of AI-enabled modernization for Canada's defence and highlight the need for Canada to adopt AI to maintain its operational advantage and interoperability with its allies. However, the DND/CAF AI Strategy provides a more detailed and specific plan for achieving AI-enabled modernization, including the creation of a DND/CAF AI Centre (DCAIC) and the development of a staged implementation plan with timelines, milestones, and performance indicators.

**Sources:**

- The Department of National Defence and Canadian Armed Forces Artificial Intelligence Strategy, pages 1-3, 6-10, 12-15, 20, 27
